## §11.1.1: *Metrische Selektortheorie*, *Strukturkompressor* (${}^4\zeta$) & *Tensorien* (SM-99) {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">STRATUM D: HISTORICAL EXEGESIS OF SELECTOR THEORY (SM §8.5, PP. 253–260, EQ. 99) &amp; DESY VIGNETTE</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.remark-box}
**Historical Vignette: The DESY Mass Computations (1982, Hamburg)**
Computer-assisted mass calculations at the German Electron Synchrotron (*Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron*, DESY) bridged Heim's coupled selector difference equations to empirical testing, generating lepton, meson, and baryon rest masses without free Yukawa parameters ($\Delta m/m < 0.1\%$ to $0.01\%$). Numerical claims remain strictly separated from the formal mathematical layer (Strata A/B) and are supplied with reproducible code in **Appendix B** and **Appendix D**.
:::

* In SM §8.5 (pp. 253–260), Heim formulates **Metrische Selektortheorie**: physical spacetime is an active geometric filter operating on *primitiv strukturierte metronische Tensorien* (SM, p. 253) generated by the cascades of Chapter 9 (${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}$, **Fundamentalkondensor** $\fundamentalkondensor \equiv \Gamma_{kl}^i$).

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**The *Strukturkompressor* (${}^4\zeta$, SM Eq. 99, p. 255) & *Tensorien* (p. 257):**
$$
\zeta_{klm}^i \coloneqq \frac{1}{\alpha_l} \partial_l \Gamma_{km}^i - \frac{1}{\alpha_m} \partial_m \Gamma_{kl}^i + \Gamma_{sl}^i \Gamma_{km}^s - \Gamma_{sm}^i \Gamma_{kl}^s \tag{SM-99}
$$
${}^4\zeta$ measures internal geometric stress, torsion, and non-linear curvature feedback. Realizable blueprint states (**Tensorien**) must satisfy operator **Eigenwertbedingungen**:
$$
\operatorname{Selector}(\Psi) = \lambda \cdot \Psi
$$
Discrete eigenvalues $\lambda$ fix inertial mass, electric charge, baryon number, and intrinsic spin.
:::

## §11.1.2: *Metronische Hyperstrukturen*, Selectors ($C_k, \chi_k, \hat{s}$) & *Geodäsie* (SM-87, SM-93a) {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">STRATUM D: METRONISIERUNGSVERFAHREN, SPIN ROTOR SELECTORS &amp; METRONISIERTE GEODÄSIE (SM §8.6, PP. 261–272)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

<h3 style="color:#5eead4; margin-top:0;">From Continuous *Tensorien* to Lattice *Hyperstrukturen*</h3>

* An abstract *Tensorion* is a continuous geometric blueprint; to manifest as a localized physical particle, it is mapped onto the discrete metronic lattice via the **Metronisierungsverfahren** (SM, p. 261), forming a **Metronische Hyperstruktur**.
* This realization is governed by three specialized filtering selectors:
  1. **Gitterselektor ($C_k$, SM, p. 264):** Enforces flat Euclidean coordinate discretization, mapping continuous $x_k$ into integer metron counts $n_k$ via $x_k = C_k ; n = \alpha_k \tau^{1/p} n_k$.
  2. **Hyperselektor ($\chi_k$, SM, p. 264):** Generalized coordinate selector for curved Riemannian configurations where ${}^2\bar{\gamma};n = {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}} \ne \text{const}$, establishing discrete geodesic mesh lines.
  3. **Spinselektoren ($\hat{s}, \hat{t}, \hat{\Phi}, {}^2\rho$, SM, pp. 265–266, Eq. 87):** Define intrinsic angular momentum and internal quantum symmetries:
$$
\hat{\mathrm{s}} = \ROT_N \widehat{\Phi} = \frac{\nabla_1 \Phi_2 - \nabla_2 \Phi_1}{\sqrt{\tau}}, \qquad (\hat{\mathrm{s}} ; \mathrm{n})_{\mathrm{n}=1} = \hat{\tau} \tag{SM-87}
$$
where $\hat{s}$ is the discrete spin rotor matrix fixing intrinsic spin $Q = 2J$ and ${}^2\rho$ is the metric selector governing spin-compatible symmetries.

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
***Metronisierte Geodäsie* (Discrete Geodesic Equation, SM Eq. 93a, p. 268):**
$$
\nabla^2 n^i + \sum_{k,l=1}^n \frac{\alpha_k\alpha_l}{\alpha_i}\nabla n^k \nabla n^l \Gamma_{kl}^i(\mathbf{n}) = 0 \tag{SM-93a}
$$
replacing continuous second derivatives with the second backward difference $\nabla^2$ (SM Eq. 68) and sampling $\Gamma_{kl}^i(\mathbf{n})$ at discrete lattice nodes.
:::

## §11.1.3: *Strukturkondensation* ($\bar{N}$) & *Null-Stabilität* (${}^4\bar{\mathbf{F}} = \mathbf{0}$, SM-91, SM-96, SM-100) {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">STRATUM D: STRUKTURKONDENSATION, METRISCHER SIEBOPERATOR &amp; RESONANT GEOMETRIC SOLITON (SM §8.7, PP. 273–279)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
***Metrischer Sieboperator* ($S(\gamma)$, SM Eq. 96) & *Strukturkondensation* ($\bar{N}$, SM Eq. 91):**
* Cascade partial structures are filtered for lattice compatibility through the **metrischer Sieboperator** $S(\gamma)$ (SM Eq. 96, p. 274), evaluating partial metric projections against the Euclidean unit baseline.
* Total realized physical order is quantified by the **Strukturkondensation** (SM Eq. 91, p. 275):
$$
\bar{N} = \mathcal{S} \bar{K} \bar{\delta} n \tag{SM-91}
$$
where $\mathcal{S}$ is the discrete summation operator (Chapter 10) and $\bar{K}$ is the effective lattice kernel section, serving as a geometric proxy for particle number and localized charge density.
:::

::: {.firewall-box .fragment .fade-right}
**The *Null-Stabilitätsbedingung* (Null Stability Condition, SM Eq. 100, p. 278):**
$$
{}^4\bar{\mathbf{F}}\!\left( \varsigma_{klm}^i, \lambda_m \begin{bmatrix} i \\ k \, l \end{bmatrix} \right)_1^N = {}^4\mathbf{0} \tag{SM-100}
$$
A physical particle is a state of **perfect internal stress cancellation**: the metronized curvature compressor ${}^4\bar{\mathbf{F}}$ vanishes identically, fixing invariant particle mass spectra and the $N=6$ subspace with multiplicities $L_p = \binom{6}{p}$ (SM Eq. 100a):
$$
m = m_0 \left(\frac{\sqrt{\tau}}{\ell_{\text{hadron}}}\right)\frac{\binom{6}{p}}{6}\prod_{k=1}^3 \lambda_k(p, \hat{s})\cdot\Big[1 - \kappa_1 q_x^2 + \kappa_n(1-|q_x|) + \kappa_2|C| + \kappa_3\mathcal{P}(\nu)\Big] \tag{SM-100a}
$$
:::

::: {.intuition-box .fragment .blur-in}
**Conceptual Bridge: From Abstract Curvature to Elementary Particle Masses**
Think of internal geometry as a musical instrument: a drum membrane vibrates only at discrete resonant harmonics. Raw metronic fields pass through the *Strukturkompressor* sieve; only configurations achieving absolute internal stress cancellation (${}^4\mathbf{F}=\mathbf{0}$) survive as *Tensorien*. Evaluated over compact $K_8$, particle rest mass ceases to be an empirical accident and becomes a topological eigenvalue locked into the crystal lattice of spacetime.
:::

## §11.2: Capacity Balance ($N=6$), 12D Fibration $R_{12}$ & Divisors (Assump. 11.1, Thm. 11.12) {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A &amp; C: CAPACITY BALANCE POLYNOMIAL (ASSUMP. 11.1), SCHOLIUM 11.2 &amp; METRON DIVISOR RULE (THM. 11.12)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.firewall-box}
**Assumption 11.1 (Heim's Combinatorial Metric Capacity Balance for $N=6$, Stratum C):**
With $\omega = N/2$, count metric-condenser capacity $Z_\omega(N)$ and coordinate-deformation capacity $Z_k(N)$ (SM, p. 297):
$$
Z_\omega(N) \coloneqq 2\binom{\omega^2}{2} + \omega^2 = \omega^4 = \frac{N^4}{16}, \qquad Z_k(N) \coloneqq N^2 + \frac{N}{2}\binom{N}{2} = \frac{N^3 + 3N^2}{4}
$$
Equating these capacities yields:
$$
\frac{N^4}{16} = \frac{N^3 + 3N^2}{4} \iff N^4 - 4N^3 - 12N^2 = N^2(N - 6)(N + 2) = 0
$$
For $N > 0$, the **unique positive solution is $N = 6$ ($\omega = 3$)**, with multiplicities $L_p = \binom{6}{p}$ (SM-100a).
:::

::: {.carnap-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Carnap Scholium 11.1 & Scholium 11.2 (Epistemic Demarcation & 12D Justification):**
* **Carnap 11.1:** The algebraic root-finding $N=6$ is exact (verified in Lean 4 below), while the capacity polynomials $Z_\omega, Z_k$ are recorded as a historical modeling assumption (**Stratum C**), not a pure category-theoretic theorem.
* **Scholium 11.2:** (1) Spectral quantization emerges from self-adjoint selectors on $L^2(\mathcal{M}, E)$; (2) $R_{12} \cong R_4 \times S_2 \times I_6$ partitions Minkowski kinematics ($R_4$), entelechial-aeonic organization ($S_2$), and internal gauge torus ($I_6$); (3) Spontaneous $N=6$ condensation locks particulate matter into $R_6 = R_4 \times S_2$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 11.12 (Metron Divisor Selection Rule, SM Eqs. 65–65a):**
If the physical dimension $N = 6$ obeys the integer quantization relation $N = pM$ with $p, M \in \mathbb{Z}^+$, then the allowed metron dimensions under that relation are:
$$
p \in \Div(6) = \{1, \, 2, \, 3, \, 6\}
$$
*(Applies strictly to the metronized subspace parameter in $N=pM$; phenomenological resonance discussions also inspect $p=4,5$ across the full Boolean hypercube $2^6 - 1 = 63$).*
:::

## §11.2.1: $R_{12} \cong R_4 \times K_8$, Hilbert Space $\mathcal{H}_E$, $\Sel$ & $\mathfrak{D}_\tau$ (Defs. 11.3–11.7) {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A: MATHEMATICAL FOUNDATIONS — 12D MANIFOLD R₁₂, HILBERT STATE SPACE H_E &amp; DISCRETIZATION FUNCTOR D_τ</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.def-box}
**Definition 11.3 (The 12-Dimensional Manifold $R_{12}$ and Boundaryless Internal Space $K_8$):**
The complete geometric arena of physical Syntrometrie is the 12D pseudo-Riemannian product fibration:
$$
R_{12} \cong R_4 \times K_8 \cong R_4 \times S^2 \times \mathbb{T}^6
$$
1. **Spacetime Sub-bundle $R_4(x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)$:** Signature $(+,+,+,-)$, observable physical 4-space.
2. **Internal Sub-bundle $K_8(x_5, \dots, x_{12}) \coloneqq S^2(x_5, x_6) \times \mathbb{T}^6(x_7, \dots, x_{12})$:** Compact, smooth, boundaryless ($\partial K_8 = \emptyset$); $S^2$ carries organizational variables ($\Delta k, t_{\text{aeon}}$) while $\mathbb{T}^6 \cong (T^2)^3$ carries internal gauge coordinates.
3. **Physical Condensation Sub-manifold:** $R_6 \coloneqq R_4 \times S_2$.
:::

::: {.def-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Definition 11.4 (Positive-Definite Euclideanized Spectral Space $\mathcal{H}_E$):**
Let $R_{12}^E \cong R_3 \times \mathbb{R}^+ \times S_2 \times I_6$ be the Wick-rotated manifold with positive-definite metric $g_E \coloneqq \operatorname{diag}(+, \dots, +)$ and vector bundle $E \to R_{12}^E$ with fiber metric $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_E$. The **Geometric State Hilbert Space** is:
$$
\mathcal{H}_E \coloneqq L^2(R_{12}^E, E) \coloneqq \left\{ \Psi \in \Gamma(R_{12}^E, E) \;\Big|\; \|\Psi\|_{L^2}^2 \coloneqq \int_{R_{12}^E} \langle \Psi(x), \Psi(x) \rangle_E \, d\vol_{g_E} < \infty \right\}
$$
Bypassing skew-symmetric torsion guarantees self-adjoint selector operators with strictly real eigenvalues.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-left}
**Definition 11.5 (Geometric Selector Operators) & Proposition 11.6 (4-Component Decomposition):**
* **Def. 11.5:** A **Geometric Selector** is a densely defined, self-adjoint linear differential operator $\Sel \colon \Dom(\Sel) \subseteq \mathcal{H}_E \to \mathcal{H}_E$ whose spectral resolution $\Sel = \int_{\sigma(\Sel)} \lambda \, dE_\lambda$ defines admissible physical states.
* **Prop. 11.6 (SM Eqs. 99a–99b, pp. 294–295):** In the metronized lattice representation, the total curvature-compression tensor decomposes into four sectors across partial structures $\alpha \in \{1, \dots, \omega\}$:
$$
{}^4\bar{\boldsymbol{\varsigma}} = \sum_{\alpha=1}^{\omega} \left( {}^4\bar{\boldsymbol{\varsigma}}(\alpha) + {}^4\bar{\mathbf{q}}(\alpha) + {}^4\bar{\mathbf{C}}(\alpha) + {}^4\bar{\mathbf{D}}(\alpha) \right) \tag{SM-99a}
$$
comprising intrinsic curvature-compression ${}^4\bar{\boldsymbol{\varsigma}}(\alpha)$, coupling ${}^4\bar{\mathbf{q}}(\alpha)$, cross-channel ${}^4\bar{\mathbf{C}}(\alpha)$, and mixed connection–coupling ${}^4\bar{\mathbf{D}}(\alpha)$.
:::

::: {.def-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Definition 11.7 (Lattice Discretization Functor $\mathfrak{D}_\tau$):**
For a discrete lattice sampling $\mathbb{M}_\tau^n \subset \mathcal{M}$, the **Lattice Discretization Map** is the bounded linear projection:
$$
\mathfrak{D}_\tau \colon C_c^\infty(\mathcal{M}, E) \longrightarrow \ell^2(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n, E), \qquad (\mathfrak{D}_\tau \Psi)(\mathbf{n}) \coloneqq \Psi\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^n n_i \tau_i e_i\right) \cdot \tau^{1/2}
$$
satisfying exact isometric continuum recovery $\lim_{\tau \to 0} \|\mathfrak{D}_\tau \Psi\|_{\ell^2} = \|\Psi\|_{L^2}$.
:::

## §11.3: Discrete Real Eigenvalues on $K_8$ & Conjectural 3-Generation Index (Thm. 11.8) {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: DISCRETE REAL EIGENVALUE THEOREM ON K₈ (THM. 11.8) &amp; CONJECTURAL 3-GENERATION DIRAC INDEX (CARNAP 11.2)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 11.8 (Discrete Real Eigenvalue Theorem on $K_8 = S^2 \times \mathbb{T}^6$):**
Let $E \to K_8$ be a smooth Hermitian vector bundle over compact, boundaryless $K_8 = S^2 \times (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^6$. Assume the geometric selector operator
$$
\Sel \;\coloneqq\; \Delta_E + \mathrm{i}\,\rho\!\left(\iota_{K_8}^*\mathbf{\Omega}_{\text{int}}^{(12)}\right) \colon H^2(K_8, E) \subset L^2(K_8, E) \longrightarrow L^2(K_8, E)
$$
is (1) strongly elliptic of 2nd order on $K_8$, (2) symmetric on $C^\infty(K_8, E)$ extending to $\Sel^\dagger = \Sel$ on $H^2(K_8, E)$, with (3) pointwise self-adjoint zero-order gauge term $\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{gauge}} \coloneqq \mathrm{i}\,\rho(\iota_{K_8}^*\mathbf{\Omega}_{\text{int}}^{(12)})$. Then:
1. $\sigma(\Sel) = \sigma_p(\Sel) = \{\lambda_k\}_{k=1}^\infty \subset \mathbb{R}$ is purely discrete, real, with $\lim_{k\to\infty}|\lambda_k| = \infty$.
2. Eigenspaces are finite-dimensional, and normalized eigenfunctions form a complete orthonormal basis of $L^2(K_8, E)$: $\Sel(\Psi_k) = \lambda_k \Psi_k, \; \langle \Psi_j, \Psi_k \rangle_{L^2} = \delta_{jk}$.

<div class="claim-ceiling-pill"><b>Claim Ceiling ($c_{\text{SEL}}$):</b> Discrete real spectra are guaranteed mathematically conditional on self-adjointness and compactness of $K_8$.</div>
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proof of Thm. 11.8 & Separated Product-Model Spectrum:**
Since $\partial K_8 = \emptyset$, integration by parts has no boundary term; $\Delta_E$ is self-adjoint and $\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{gauge}}$ preserves self-adjointness by Kato–Rellich. By Rellich's Compact Embedding ($H^2(K_8,E) \hookrightarrow L^2(K_8,E)$ compact) and elliptic regularity, $(\Sel - zI)^{-1}$ is compact, yielding a discrete real eigenbasis. For $A = -\Delta_{K_8} + V_0$ on $K_8 = S^2(R_S) \times \prod_{a=1}^6 S^1_{L_a}$, separated eigenfunctions $Y_\ell^{m_S}\prod L_a^{-1/2}e^{2\pi i m_a\theta_a/L_a}\otimes v_\alpha$ have exact eigenvalues:
$$
\lambda_{\ell,\mathbf{m},\alpha} = \frac{\ell(\ell+1)}{R_S^2} + \sum_{a=1}^6 \frac{4\pi^2 m_a^2}{L_a^2} + \mu_\alpha \qquad \blacksquare
$$
:::

## §11.3 & App. B (§B.5): Centered Staggered Lattice Geodesics & Verlet Precession {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B &amp; C: STAGGERED GEODESIC DIFFERENCE SYSTEM (DEF. 11.9), CONDENSATION (DEF. 11.10) &amp; VERLET ORBITS (DEF. B.8, PROP. B.9)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.def-box}
**Definition 11.9 (Centered Staggered Discrete Lattice Geodesic System, SM-93a):**
To align discrete 1-link velocities $\nabla n^k(m) = n^k(m) - n^k(m-1)$ with discrete acceleration $\nabla^2 n^i(m)$ at second-order accuracy $\mathcal{O}(\tau^2)$ on $\mathbb{M}_\tau^n$:
1. **Centered Cell-Average Operator $\mu \colon \ell^\infty(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n) \to \ell^\infty(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n)$:**
$$
\mu n^k(m) \coloneqq \frac{1}{2}\big(n^k(m) + n^k(m-1)\big)
$$
2. **Centered Discrete Geodesic Difference Equation:**
$$
\nabla^2 n^i(m) + \sum_{k,l=1}^n \frac{\alpha_k \alpha_l}{\alpha_i}\big(\nabla n^k(m)\big)\big(\nabla n^l(m)\big)\!\left[\frac{\Gamma_{kl}^i(\mathbf{n}(m)) + \Gamma_{kl}^i(\mathbf{n}(m-1))}{2}\right] = 0 \tag{SM-93a}
$$
evaluating $\Gamma_{kl}^i$ at the midpoint of the step to eliminate grid-staggering phase errors.
:::

::: {.def-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Definition 11.10 (Structural Condensation Functional) & Def. B.8 (Symplectic Verlet Stencil):**
* **Def. 11.10 (SM-91):** For effective lattice kernel section $\widetilde{K} \in \ell^1(\mathbb{M}_\tau^n)$, total condensed structural information is $\bar{N} \coloneqq \mathcal{S}\widetilde{K} = \sum_{\mathbf{n}\in\mathbb{M}_\tau^n} \widetilde{K}(\mathbf{n}) < \infty$.
* **Def. B.8 & Alg. D.2 (Central Verlet Stencil on $\mathbb{M}_\tau^4$):** Unfolding $\nabla^2 n^i(m)$ yields the explicit area-preserving update:
$$
n^i(m+1) = 2n^i(m) - n^i(m-1) - \sum_{k,l=1}^4 \frac{\alpha_k\alpha_l}{\alpha_i}\big(n^k(m)-n^k(m-1)\big)\big(n^l(m)-n^l(m-1)\big)\Gamma_{kl}^i(\mathbf{n}(m))
$$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proposition B.9 (Orbital Precession & Light Deflection on Discrete Lattices, Figs. B.2–B.3):**
In the Schwarzschild–Heim metric $g_{00} = -(1 - \frac{2GM}{c^2 r}), \; g_{rr} = (1 - \frac{2GM}{c^2 r})^{-1}$, numerical integration reproduces Mercury's perihelion advance $\Delta\phi = \frac{6\pi GM}{c^2 a(1-e^2)} = 42.98''/\text{century}$ with error $\mathcal{O}(\tau/r^2) < 10^{-40}$ and gravitational light bending $\delta\theta = \frac{4GM}{c^2 b} + \mathcal{O}(\tau/b^2)$, while eliminating $r\to 0$ continuum singularities via the minimum cell cutoff $r_{\min} \ge \sqrt{\tau}$.
:::

## §11.3: Geometric Mass-Ratio Theorem & 63-Channel Hyper-Lattice (Thm. 11.11, SM-100a) {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: THE GEOMETRIC MASS-RATIO THEOREM (THM. 11.11) &amp; 63-CHANNEL BOOLEAN HYPERCUBE PARTITION (FIGS. 11.5–11.7)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 11.11 (The Geometric Mass-Ratio Theorem, SM Eq. 100a):**
Let $\Sel$ be a self-adjoint selector operator on $L_w^2(K_8, E)$ with discrete real point spectrum $\Spec(\Sel) = \{\lambda_k\}_{k=1}^\infty$.
1. **Dimensionless Eigenvalue Ratio:** The mass ratio $\mu(p, \hat{s}) \coloneqq m(p, \hat{s}) / m_{\mathrm{ref}}$ of any particle state to a reference ground state ($e^-$ or $p$) is a **purely geometric dimensionless ratio**:
$$
\frac{m(p, \hat{s})}{m_{\mathrm{ref}}} \;=\; \frac{\binom{6}{p}}{\binom{6}{p_{\mathrm{ref}}}} \cdot \prod_{k=1}^3 \left( \frac{\lambda_k(p, \hat{s})}{\lambda_k(p_{\mathrm{ref}}, \hat{s}_{\mathrm{ref}})} \right) \cdot \frac{\mathcal{C}(q_x, C, \nu)}{\mathcal{C}(q_{x,\mathrm{ref}}, C_{\mathrm{ref}}, \nu_{\mathrm{ref}})} \tag{SM-100a}
$$
which is strictly non-circular and independent of the proton Compton wavelength $\ell_{\text{hadron}}$.
2. **Bridge Hypothesis ($\mathbf{C}$):** The absolute physical mass scale is parameterized by the single global geometric ratio $\xi_{\text{scale}} \coloneqq \sqrt{\tau} / \ell_{\text{ref}}$.
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Proof of Theorem 11.11 & Worked Example ($L_p = \binom{6}{p}$, Def. B.5):**
* **Step 1:** Vanishing of ${}^4\bar{\mathbf{F}}(\varsigma_{klm}^i, \lambda_m\Gamma_{kl}^i) = {}^4\mathbf{0}$ on $R_6$ restricts metric fluctuations to eigenspaces of $\Sel_k$.
* **Step 2:** Integrated volume condensation $\bar{N} = \mathcal{S}\bar{K}$ factors into combinatorial sub-tensor channel weights $L_p = \binom{6}{p}$ normalized by base channel $L_1 = \binom{6}{1} = 6$:
$$
\mathbf{L} = \left(\binom{6}{1}, \binom{6}{2}, \binom{6}{3}, \binom{6}{4}, \binom{6}{5}, \binom{6}{6}\right) = (6, \, 15, \, 20, \, 15, \, 6, \, 1), \quad \sum_{p=1}^6 \binom{6}{p} = 2^6 - 1 = \mathbf{63}
$$
* **Step 3:** Multiplying by the discrete spin-rotor eigenvalues $\prod_{k=1}^3 \lambda_k(p, \hat{s})$ yields SM-100a. $\blacksquare$
:::

## App. B (§B.1–B.2): Fundamental Metron Scale ($\tau, m_0$) & 6D State Vector $\mathbf{q}_{\mathrm{Heim}}$ {.smaller transition="convex"}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.firewall-box}
**Scholium B.1 (Metron Scale Arithmetic and Physical Demarcation):**
Applying CODATA constants ($\hbar \approx 1.054571817\times 10^{-34}\,\mathrm{J\cdot s}$, $G \approx 6.67430\times 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{m^3 kg^{-1} s^{-2}}$, $c \approx 2.99792458\times 10^8\,\mathrm{m/s}$):
$$
\ell_P^2 \coloneqq \frac{\hbar G}{c^3} \approx 2.61223 \times 10^{-70}\,\mathrm{m}^2, \qquad \tau_{\text{derived}} \coloneqq \frac{\sqrt{3}\hbar G}{4c^3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\ell_P^2 = \mathbf{1.13115 \times 10^{-70}\,\mathrm{m}^2}
$$
$$
\boxed{\text{Correct Arithmetic} \neq \text{Correct Formula} \neq \text{Correct Physical Realization}}
$$
*(Note: $\tau_{\text{historical}} \approx 4.05\times 10^{-70}\,\mathrm{m}^2$ in secondary literature uses an alternative normalization prefactor; this monograph sets $\tau_{\text{derived}} = 1.13115\times 10^{-70}\,\mathrm{m}^2$ as its unified $\mathbf{S_2}$ baseline).*
:::

::: {.def-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Definition B.2 (The Base Metronic Mass Unit $m_0$, Stratum C Bridge):**
The formal base metronic mass scale $m_0$ is the Compton mass associated with $\sqrt{\tau_{\text{derived}}}$:
$$
m_0 \coloneqq \frac{\hbar}{c\sqrt{\tau_{\text{derived}}}} = \left(\frac{4\hbar c}{\sqrt{3}G}\right)^{1/2} \approx \mathbf{3.308 \times 10^{-8}\,\mathrm{kg}} \approx \mathbf{1.855 \times 10^{19}\,\mathrm{GeV}/c^2}
$$
Physical rest masses are discrete fractional sub-multiples of $m_0$ filtered through $\Sel$.
:::

::: {.def-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Definition B.4 (Exact Numerical DESY Mass Perturbation Parameters):**
$$
\begin{aligned}
\ell_{\text{hadron}} &\coloneqq \frac{\hbar}{m_p c} \approx \mathbf{2.103089 \times 10^{-16}\,\mathrm{m}}, & \kappa_1 &\coloneqq \mathbf{0.000543} \;\;(\text{Coulomb Self-Energy on }x_5)\\
\kappa_n &\coloneqq \mathbf{0.001378} \;\;(\text{Isospin Bias } m_n > m_p), & \kappa_2 &\coloneqq \mathbf{0.001210} \;\;(\text{Strangeness/Charm } |C|)\\
\kappa_3 &\coloneqq \mathbf{0.000852} \;\;(\text{Radial Multiplet Mode}), & \mathcal{P}(\nu) &\coloneqq (\nu - 1) + 7.42(\nu - 1)^3
\end{aligned}
$$

::: {.thm-box}
**Definition B.3 (The 6-Dimensional Particle State Vector $\mathbf{q}_{\text{Heim}}$):**
Every stationary *Metronische Hyperstruktur* on $R_6 = R_4 \times S_2$ is uniquely classified by a 6-component integer/half-integer quantum state tuple:
$$
\mathbf{q}_{\text{Heim}} \;\coloneqq\; \big( k, \; P, \; Q, \; \nu, \; C, \; q_x \big)
$$
1. **$k \in \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ (Configuration Grade / Cascade Tier):**
   * $k=1$: Leptonic bare states (single-channel geometry, $L_1 = 6$).
   * $k=2$: Mesonic 2-flux bound states ($L_2 = 15$).
   * $k=3$: Baryonic 3-flux nucleon & hyperon states ($L_3 = 20$).
   * $k=4$: Excited heavy resonance states ($L_4 = 15$).
2. **$P \coloneqq 2I \in \mathbb{N}_0$ (Double Isospin):** $I \in \{0, 1/2, 1, 3/2\}$.
3. **$Q \coloneqq 2J \in \mathbb{N}_0$ (Double Spatial Spin):** $J \in \{0, 1/2, 1, 3/2\}$ from $\hat{s} = \ROT_N\widehat{\Phi}$.
4. **$\nu \in \mathbb{N}$ (Radial Multiplet / Excitation Index):** Principal harmonic mode in $\mathcal{P}(\nu)$.
5. **$C \in \mathbb{Z}$ (Structure Distributor):** Geometrization of strangeness, charm, and hypercharge.
6. **$q_x \in \{-1, 0, +1\}$ (Electric Charge Quantum Number):** Parity coupling between $R_4$ and entelechial coordinate $x_5$.

* **Neutron $n^0$ ($k=3, L_3=20, q_x=0, C=0, \nu=1$):** Activates the neutral isospin exchange bias $+\kappa_n(1-|q_x|) = +0.001378$, lifting the neutral nucleon above the proton ground state to $m_n = \mathbf{939.5654\,\mathrm{MeV}/c^2}$ ($\Delta m_{n-p} = \mathbf{+1.293\,\mathrm{MeV}} > 0$)!
